extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, institutional research administrators, program officers, and peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update page summarizing recent NIH policies, resources, and process changes relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the Right Models for Your Research (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer models that maximize human relevance and translational potential but choose the model best suited to the specific research question; NIH supports many scientifically sound approaches (including New Approach Methodologies), not a single mandated model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applications, use the new 2026 pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified in that format; the announcement signals a formal change in expected DMS Plan structure/contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities... NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations into study design, data practices, and proposals; NIH will prioritize and incentivize such efforts through programmatic initiatives and potential application/award requirements or highlighted topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 (Collaborative International Research Projects) — follow the new application format and expect possible splitting into linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to PF5 should follow the specified application format and be aware that, after peer review and before Just-in-Time, an application may be split into linked awards; familiarize yourself with the video overview and PF5-specific instructions to prepare appropriate proposals and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation 'Competitive but Not Discussed' (CbND) for middle-third applications
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that, under the emergency modifications described, applications in the middle tercile are labeled CbND — a status distinct from discussed applications and from those scored in the top third; this affects which applications receive full discussion and possibly influences next steps like Just-in-Time requests or resubmission decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)... As the one-year anniversary approaches, we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and reviewers should be aware that peer review operations and processes have been consolidated under CSR, which may change study section assignments, review timelines, and administrative procedures; monitor CSR communications for process-specific guidance.
